Your job is to help developers understand and use ChatCops — an open-source AI chatbot widget.

Key facts:
- ChatCops has 3 packages: @chatcops/widget (client), @chatcops/server (backend), @chatcops/core (providers/tools)
- Widget is zero-dependency, Shadow DOM isolated, and works with a single script tag
- Server supports Express, Vercel, and Cloudflare Workers

Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: How do I install ChatCops?
A: The easiest way is via CDN: add a <script> tag with src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@chatcops/widget@1/dist/chatcops.min.js" and set data-api-url to your server endpoint. For npm: install @chatcops/widget, @chatcops/server, and optionally @chatcops/core.

Q: Is ChatCops free?
A: Yes! ChatCops is fully open-source under the MIT license. You only pay for your AI provider API usage (e.g., Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google).

Q: What is ChatCops?
A: ChatCops is an open-source, universal AI chatbot widget you can embed on any website with a single script tag. It supports Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini as AI providers.

Q: What AI providers are supported?
A: ChatCops supports Claude (Anthropic), OpenAI, and Google Gemini. You configure the provider and model on the server side — the widget is provider-agnostic.

Q: What server platforms are supported?
A: ChatCops has adapters for Express.js, Vercel Serverless/Edge Functions, and Cloudflare Workers. You can also build custom integrations using the core package.

<source id="2" url="https://chat.codercops.com/examples/vercel-full/" title="Vercel Edge Full Example" section="API Route (`api/chat.ts`)">
Vercel Edge Full Example > API Route (`api/chat.ts`)

```typescript
import { chatcopsVercelHandler } from '@chatcops/server';
import { LeadCaptureTool, FAQKnowledgeSource } from '@chatcops/core';

export const config = { runtime: 'edge' };

export default chatcopsVercelHandler({
  provider: {
    type: 'claude',
    apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY!,
    model: 'claude-haiku-5-5',
  },

  systemPrompt: `You are a helpful AI assistant for our SaaS product.
    Answer questions about features, pricing, and getting started.
    If a user shares contact info, capture it with the lead tool.`,

  tools: [
    new LeadCaptureTool(async (lead) => {
      // Send to webhook (e.g., Zapier, Make, n8n)
      await fetch(process.env.WEBHOOK_URL!, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          type: 'lead_captured',
          lead,
          timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        }),
      });
    }),
  ],

  knowledge: [
    new FAQKnowledgeSource([
      { question: 'What is your pricing?', answer: 'Starter: Free, Pro: $29/mo, Enterprise: Custom.' },
      { question: 'Is there a free trial?', answer: 'Yes, 14-day free trial on all paid plans.' },
      { question: 'What integrations do you support?', answer: 'Slack, Discord, Zapier, webhooks, and REST API.' },
    ]),
  ],

  allowedOrigins: ['*'],
  sessionSecrets: [process.env.CHATCOPS_SESSION_SECRET!],
  analytics: true,
});
```

Add `api/chat/session.ts` with `export { default, config } from '../chat';`, so `/api/chat/session`, where the widget gets its session token, reaches the same handler.
</source>
<source id="3" url="https://chat.codercops.com/getting-started/test-before-launch/" title="Test Before Launch" section="4. Run replays in CI for free">
Test Before Launch > 4. Run replays in CI for free

When the `CI` environment variable is set (which GitHub Actions and most CI systems set automatically), `chatcops test` replays by default. You do not need to configure any API keys or secrets in your CI environment.

Add a GitHub Actions workflow at `.github/workflows/evals.yml`:

```yaml
name: Evals
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  evals:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 22 }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx chatcops test
```

Because `CI=true` triggers `--replay`, the entire test suite executes in milliseconds on every pull request. If a PR modifies the system prompt without updating the cassettes, CI fails, prompting the author to verify the change locally with `--record`.
</source>
<source id="4" url="https://chat.codercops.com/server/ai-sdk/" title="AI SDK (useChat)">
AI SDK (useChat)

`chatcopsAiSdkHandler` answers in the [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev)'s UI message stream, so an app that already uses `useChat` can use a ChatCops server instead of its own route. You keep your chat UI and get ChatCops on the server: stored conversations, rate limits, budgets, allowed origins and tools.

It's a Fetch API handler like `chatcopsVercelHandler`, so it works as a Next.js route handler and in any runtime from the [fetch runtimes page](/server/fetch-runtimes/). It's tested against `ai` 7.
</source>
<source id="5" url="https://chat.codercops.com/widget/react/" title="React" section="`useChatCops()` Hook">
React > `useChatCops()` Hook

`useChatCops()` returns an object with helper methods to control the widget:

```tsx
const chat = useChatCops();
```

| Method | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `chat.open()` | `() => void` | Opens the chat panel. |
| `chat.close()` | `() => void` | Closes the chat panel. |
| `chat.toggle()` | `() => void` | Toggles the chat panel open or closed. |
| `chat.send(text, options?)` | `(text: string, options?: { open?: boolean }) => Promise<void>` | Sends a message as the visitor. Opens the chat by default unless `open: false` is passed. Resolves when the assistant reply finishes streaming. |
| `chat.update(changes)` | `(changes: WidgetUpdate) => void` | Updates theme, branding, or strings on the active chat. |

Before the widget bundle has loaded on the client, these methods safely do nothing (`send()` returns a resolved promise).
</source>

<source id="1" url="https://chat.codercops.com/core/tools/" title="Tools" section="Built-in: Lead Capture">
Tools > Built-in: Lead Capture

The `LeadCaptureTool` lets the AI collect contact information from conversations:

```typescript
import { LeadCaptureTool } from '@chatcops/core';

const leadTool = new LeadCaptureTool(async (lead) => {
  console.log('New lead:', lead);
  // Save to database, CRM, send webhook, etc.
});
```

<source id="2" url="https://chat.codercops.com/getting-started/test-before-launch/" title="Test Before Launch" section="1. Write your first eval file">
Test Before Launch > 1. Write your first eval file

By default, `chatcops test` looks for any `evals/**/*.chat.yaml` file. Create a file at `evals/launch.chat.yaml`.

Pick three to five questions your bot must get right before going live. A good starting suite covers your pricing tiers, lead capture, and an off-topic request your bot should decline:

```yaml
version: 1
name: Pre-launch Bot Verification
tests:
  - name: quotes Starter and Pro plan pricing
    tags: [pricing]
    turns:
      - user: How much do your plans cost?
        expect:
          - contains: ["Starter", "$29", "Pro", "$79"]

  - name: captures a sales lead
    tags: [leads]
    turns:
      - user: I would like an enterprise demo. My name is Alex, email is alex@example.com, and we need SSO with 50 seats.
        expect:
          - calls-tool: capture_lead
          - lead-captured: true

  - name: politely declines off-topic requests
    tags: [guardrails]
    turns:
      - user: Can you write me a poem about the ocean?
        expect:
          - judge: "Politely declines and steers the visitor back to Acme's products."
```

Each item under `expect` is an assertion with a single key:

- `contains`: Checks that one or more strings appear in the bot's reply. Passing a list (`["Starter", "$29"]`) ensures all of them appear.
- `calls-tool`: Confirms the bot invoked a tool during the turn (such as `capture_lead`). You can also specify arguments to check: `calls-tool: { name: capture_lead, args: { email: alex@example.com } }`.
- `lead-captured`: Checks that the turn emitted a captured lead (from `LeadCaptureTool`). You can pass `true` to ensure any lead was captured, or an object such as `lead-captured: { email: alex@example.com }` to match specific fields.
- `judge`: Asks a second model (the judge) to evaluate the reply against a natural-language rubric from 0 to 1. The test passes when the score reaches `threshold` (0.7 by default). This is ideal for open-ended guidelines like staying polite or refusing out-of-scope tasks.
</source>

Widget Configuration > WidgetConfig Interface

```typescript
// docs-check: skip, a reference listing rather than code to run
interface WidgetConfig {
  apiUrl: string;
  nonce?: string;                // CSP nonce for the widget's injected styles
  timeout?: number;              // Inactivity timeout in ms, default: 30000
  turnstileSiteKey?: string;     // Cloudflare Turnstile site key, when the server has `turnstile` set
  userToken?: string | (() => string | undefined | Promise<string | undefined>); // Your server's signed token for a signed-in visitor (server `identity`), or a function that returns a fresh one

  // Display mode
  mode?: 'popup' | 'inline';       // Default: 'popup'
  container?: string | HTMLElement; // Required when mode is 'inline'
  siteId?: string;                 // Names the saved conversation; set one per widget when a page has several

  theme?: {
    mode?: 'light' | 'dark' | 'auto';  // Default: 'auto', which follows the system setting
    accent?: string;          // Hex color, default: '#4f46e5' (light), '#6366f1' (dark)
    accentDark?: string;      // Hex color, the accent in dark mode. Default: accent
    textColor?: string;       // Hex color, replaces the text color in every mode
    bgColor?: string;         // Hex color, replaces the background in every mode
    fontFamily?: string;      // CSS font-family
    borderRadius?: string | number;  // px if a number or numeric string (12, '12'), or any CSS length ('1rem'). Default: 12
    position?: 'bottom-right' | 'bottom-left';
  };

  branding?: {
    name?: string;            // Header title
    avatar?: string;          // URL or data URI
    subtitle?: string;        // Below title in header
  };

  welcomeMessage?: string;    // First assistant message
  disclosure?: false | {      // The "you're chatting with an AI" note, on by default
    text?: string;            // Replaces the wording
    learnMoreUrl?: string;    // Adds a "Learn more" link (http or https)
  };
  suggestions?: string[];     // Suggested question buttons shown in a new conversation
  welcomeBubble?: {           // Popup mode only
    text: string;             // Text shown on hover bubble
    delay?: number;           // ms before bubble appears, 0 to 2147483647 (about 24.8 days), default: 3000. A larger number waits that long; NaN, a negative or a non-number uses the default
    showOnce?: boolean;       // Show only once (default: true): per browser with 'local' persistence, per tab with 'session', every page load with 'none'
  };
  placeholder?: string;       // Input placeholder text
  persistence?: 'local' | 'session' | 'none'; // Where the chat is saved, default: 'local'
  historyTtlDays?: number;    // Drop saved chats older than this, default: 30
  waitForConsent?: boolean;   // Show a notice and use no storage or API until setConsent(true), default: false
  onConsentRequest?: () => void; // The notice's button; leave it out to have no button
  maxMessages?: number;       // Max messages to persist, default: 50
  pageContext?: boolean;       // Send page URL/title, default: true

  privacyUrl?: string;        // Link in header menu to your site's privacy policy (https: or http: only)
  preChatForm?: {
    enabled: boolean;
    title?: string;
    subtitle?: string;
    submitLabel?: string;
    fields: Array<{
      name: string;
      type: 'text' | 'email' | 'select' | 'textarea';
      label: string;
      placeholder?: string;
      required?: boolean;
      options?: string[];

<source id="3" url="https://chat.codercops.com/widget/theming/" title="Theming" section="Light, dark and auto">
Theming > Light, dark and auto

The widget has a light and a dark look. By default (`mode: 'auto'`) it follows the visitor's system setting, and switches while the page is open when that setting changes. Pin one with `mode`:

```typescript
ChatCops.init({
  apiUrl: '/api/chat',
  theme: {
    mode: 'light',               // 'light', 'dark' or 'auto' (the default)
    accent: '#4f46e5',           // buttons, the launcher, visitor messages
    accentDark: '#a5b4fc',       // the accent in dark mode; defaults to accent
    fontFamily: 'Inter, sans-serif',
    borderRadius: 12,            // px if a number, or any CSS length like '1rem'
    tokens: {
      border: '#d0d4da',
      'panel-width': '440px',
    },
    position: 'bottom-right',    // or 'bottom-left'
  },
});
```

On the script tag, these are `data-theme-mode`, `data-accent` and `data-accent-dark`.

| Element | Light | Dark |
|---------|-------|------|
| Background | `#ffffff` | `#0a0a0a` |
| Surface (bot messages, header) | `#f4f5f7` | `#1a1a1a` |
| Input area | `#ffffff` | `#2a2a2a` |
| Border | `#d9dce1` | `#333333` |
| Text | `#1a1d23` | `#ffffff` |
| Secondary text | `#5b616e` | `#a0a0a0` |
| Accent | `#4f46e5` | `#6366f1` |
| Errors | `#c62828` | `#ef4444` |

The dark look is the one the widget had before light mode existed. Text on the accent is picked for contrast (white or near-black, with the accent darkened a little when neither reaches 4.5:1), in each mode for its own accent.
</source>
<source id="4" url="https://chat.codercops.com/widget/configuration/" title="Widget Configuration" section="Programmatic Configuration > AI disclosure">
Widget Configuration > Programmatic Configuration > AI disclosure

A new conversation starts with a short note: "You're chatting with an AI assistant. It can make mistakes." The EU AI Act (Article 50) asks that people know when they're talking to an AI, and the note stays at the top of the chat, also after "New conversation". Its strings are `disclosure` and `disclosureLearnMore` in the locale, and a language that doesn't have them yet shows them in English.

Change the wording, or add a link to a page that explains more:

```typescript
ChatCops.init({
  apiUrl: '/api/chat',
  disclosure: {
    text: 'Acme Assistant is an AI. It can get things wrong, so check anything important.',
    learnMoreUrl: 'https://acme.com/ai',
  },
});
```

`disclosure: false` (or `data-disclosure="false"`) removes it. The widget then logs a note in the console, because telling visitors some other way is up to you.
</source>

Q: How do I install ChatCops?

<source id="1" url="https://chat.codercops.com/core/providers/" title="AI Providers">
AI Providers

ChatCops puts every provider behind the same `AIProvider` interface. Switch between Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini by changing one config value.

<source id="2" url="https://chat.codercops.com/core/providers/" title="AI Providers" section="Default models">
AI Providers > Default models

| Provider | Default model | SDK | Streaming |
|----------|---------------|-----|-----------|
| Claude | `claude-haiku-5-5` | `@anthropic-ai/sdk` | `messages.stream()` |
| OpenAI | `gpt-5-mini` | `openai` | `chat.completions.create({ stream: true })` |
| Gemini | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `@google/genai` | `models.generateContentStream()` |

Set `model` to use any other model the provider offers.
</source>
<source id="3" url="https://chat.codercops.com/core/providers/" title="AI Providers" section="Direct provider usage">
AI Providers > Direct provider usage

To use a provider outside the server, create it from the same config and run a turn with it (see [Running a turn](#running-a-turn) below):

```typescript
import { createProvider } from '@chatcops/core';

const provider = await createProvider({
  type: 'claude',
  apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY!,
});
```

The provider classes aren't exported from `@chatcops/core`, so importing core doesn't load all three SDKs. Import them from their own paths:

```typescript
import { ClaudeProvider } from '@chatcops/core/providers/claude';
import { OpenAIProvider } from '@chatcops/core/providers/openai';
import { GeminiProvider } from '@chatcops/core/providers/gemini';

const provider = new ClaudeProvider({ type: 'claude', apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY! });
```
</source>

<source id="5" url="https://chat.codercops.com/core/providers/" title="AI Providers" section="Options">
AI Providers > Options

| Option | Providers | Default | What it does |
|--------|-----------|---------|--------------|
| `type` | all | none | `'claude'`, `'openai'`, `'gemini'`, `'openai-compatible'`, or the name of a [custom provider](#custom-providers). |
| `apiKey` | all | none | Required for Claude, OpenAI and Gemini. Optional for `openai-compatible`. |
| `model` | all | see above | The model id. Required for `openai-compatible`. |
| `effort` | all | `'low'` | How much effort the model spends per reply: `'low'`, `'medium'`, `'high'`, `'xhigh'` or `'max'`. Lower is faster and cheaper, which suits chat. Sent as `output_config.effort` to Claude 4.6 and later, `reasoning_effort` to OpenAI reasoning models, and `thinkingLevel` to Gemini 3 models. Models without an effort setting ignore it. |
| `baseURL` | all | provider default | A custom API endpoint: a proxy, a gateway, or an OpenAI-compatible server. Required for `openai-compatible`. |
| `headers` | OpenAI, openai-compatible | none | Extra headers sent on every request. |
| `supportsTools` | OpenAI, openai-compatible | `true` | Set to `false` for a model that can't call tools. Tools aren't sent, and one warning is logged. |
| `fetch` | all | the global `fetch` | The `fetch` the provider SDK sends requests with. Use it to route requests through a proxy, or to replay recorded responses in tests. |
| `promptCaching` | Claude | `true` | Marks the system prompt and tools as a cached prefix, so later requests read them from Claude's prompt cache at about a tenth of the input price. Prompts shorter than the model's cache minimum aren't cached either way. OpenAI and Gemini cache long prompts on their own. |
| `organization` | OpenAI | none | Your OpenAI organization id. |
| `maxTokensParam` | OpenAI, openai-compatible | `'max_completion_tokens'` for `openai`, `'max_tokens'` for `openai-compatible` | The name of the output token limit sent to the API. |

import { createProvider } from '@chatcops/core';

  type: 'gemini',
  apiKey: process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY!,
  model: 'gemini-3.5-flash-lite', // optional: override default
});
```
(Provider classes can also be instantiated directly if needed — see the docs) [3][1].

Make sure your server forwards the widget’s requests to this provider and that you set the widget’s data-api-url to your server endpoint. See the AI Providers docs for full options and examples [1][2].

ChatCopsBot

If you saw `ChatCopsBot` in your server logs, a site is building a search index for its ChatCops chat assistant with [`@chatcops/ingest`](/core/knowledge-base/#building-an-index-from-your-site). ChatCops is open source software that each site runs itself, so the requests come from whoever is running it, not from a central ChatCops service. Usually that's you, or someone indexing a site they look after.

The user agent looks like this:

```
ChatCopsBot/0.1 (+https://chat.codercops.com/bot)
```
</source>

<source id="4" url="https://chat.codercops.com/core/testing/" title="Testing your bot" section="Unit tests with a scripted model > Testing a store">
Testing your bot > Unit tests with a scripted model > Testing a store

If you write your own storage, `runStorageConformance` runs the checks every built-in store passes. It covers saving and appending, version conflicts, counters, expiry, events and, when the store has `vectors`, vector search:

```typescript
import { runStorageConformance } from '@chatcops/core/testing';
import { memoryStorage } from '@chatcops/core';

runStorageConformance('my store', () => memoryStorage(), { ttlMs: 1500 });
```

Call it at the top level of a Vitest file. `ttlMs` (150 by default) is the expiry the checks use, and they wait about twice that, so raise it for a backend that rounds expiry to seconds. `skip` leaves out checks a backend can't meet in a test run: `'kv-ttl'`, `'counter-ttl'`, `'conversation-concurrency'`, `'counter-concurrency'` or `'vector-keyword-cjk'`. For example, Workers KV's shortest TTL is 60 seconds, so skip `'kv-ttl'` there.
</source>

<conversation>
Visitor: Is there a WordPress plugin for ChatCops?
Assistant: Short answer: No — there isn’t an official WordPress plugin for ChatCops right now. 

That said, it’s very easy to add ChatCops to a WordPress site:

- Easiest: add the widget script tag to your theme’s header/footer (or use a plugin like “Insert Headers and Footers”):
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@chatcops/widget@1/dist/chatcops.min.js" data-api-url="https://your-chatcops-server.example/api"></script>
  Make sure data-api-url points to your ChatCops server endpoint.

- Slightly more robust: create a tiny custom WP plugin (or a mu-plugin) that enqueues that script or injects it into wp_head/wp_footer, so it survives theme updates.

- If you need deeper integration (server-side lead capture, events, or custom auth), run the @chatcops/server backend and connect it to your site as usual.

Repo and docs: github.com/codercops/chatcops — you’ll find examples for the widget and server there.

If you want, tell me whether you prefer injecting the script or building a small plugin and I’ll give the exact code/snippet for WordPress.
</conversation>
